milestone.title: raul TUI compute-then-render: ViewState, hit area pre-computation

intent.outcome: raul's TUI separates geometry (compute_view) from drawing (render) so layout is computed once per frame and reused by both the renderer and the mouse-handler. Adding a new clickable region, scrollable list, or modal becomes a one-place change in ViewState, not a four-file scavenger hunt across render.rs and runner.rs.

problem.description: Today, render() in crates/raul/src/tui/render.rs:340+ both computes layout AND draws in the same pass. Tab hit areas are recomputed in the mouse handler in runner.rs separately from the render pass — this was patched in M105 by adding a shared TabBarLayout, but the underlying coupling remains: pub fn tab_text_width / pub fn visible_tab_x_ranges are pub solely for cross-module access between runner and render, leaking layout internals. There is no single source of truth for 'where is each interactive element on screen this frame'. When adding a new list, board, or overlay, every one needs hit-test data recomputed in two places, which is exactly the kind of duplication that produces off-by-one bugs and stale hit areas. herdr's src/app/state.rs defines a ViewState pre-computed in compute_view() that holds ALL hit areas (workspace_card_areas, tab_hit_areas, pane_infos, toast_hit_area) and is read by both render and input dispatch — a clean pattern that scales.

in_scope: New module crates/raul/src/tui/view_state.rs defining ViewState struct with: tab_hit_areas, list_item_rects (per active list, by stable item id), board_column_rects, board_card_rects, overlay_rect (when modal/help open), scrollbar_rects (placeholder, populated in M137)
New fn compute_view(app: &App, area: Rect) -> ViewState called once at the top of the render pass and once on the mouse-handler path (or passed in to it)
Refactor render() so it takes (&App, &ViewState, frame) — pure reads, no geometry mutation
Refactor mouse handler in runner.rs to read hit areas from the pre-computed ViewState instead of recomputing tab_text_width / visible_tab_x_ranges inline
Make pub fn tab_text_width / pub fn visible_tab_x_ranges / pub fn compute_tab_bar_layout private to render.rs (or the new view_state.rs) — no more cross-module leakage
Tests: ViewState for a known app state and area produces deterministic rects; rect for each interactive element matches what render() drew (golden test or area-equality test)
out_of_scope: Mode enum dispatch (next milestone M136) — ViewState is data; dispatch logic is separate
Scrollbar widget itself (M137) — only the rect slot is reserved here
Custom widgets beyond ratatui Paragraph / Block / Layout — no cell-level buffer writes
Async I/O, animation timer, render profiler — separate concerns

work_packages.name: ViewState struct + compute_view

work_packages.name: render() refactor

work_packages.name: Mouse handler refactor

steps.action: Create crates/raul/src/tui/view_state.rs with ViewState struct: tab_hit_areas (Vec<(TabId, Rect)>), list_item_rects, board_column_rects, board_card_rects, overlay_rect (Option<Rect>), scrollbar_rects (placeholder, populated in M137).

steps.action: Implement compute_view(app: &App, area: Rect) -> ViewState. Walks the active tab, the active list, the board, and any active overlay; populates all hit rects. Pure read of App; no mutation.

findings.description: drift: S4 done_when said 'The three former pub fns are no longer pub.' The cross-module leak to runner.rs is fixed (handle_mouse reads view.tab_hit_areas), but the three functions (tab_text_width, compute_tab_bar_layout, visible_tab_x_ranges) are still pub — re-exported from render.rs as 'pub use super::view_state::{...}' for backward compat with tui_mouse.rs and tab_bar_narrow_width.rs integration tests, and still declared pub in view_state.rs itself. Strictly violates the S4 done_when. Resolution: either move the M105 / M124 layout tests to #[cfg(test)] mod tests inside view_state.rs (then they can access pub(super) items) and tighten the re-exports, OR amend the spec's S4 done_when to 'no longer pub from render.rs' (the cross-module leak target). Filed as spec-gap, see dogfood entry 21 for the verification-text trip that prompted the broader visibility audit.

M135's stated goal (L41: render and hit-test must share the same layout) is only fully closed for the TAB BAR. handle_mouse (runner.rs:581) computes the ViewState but then, for the list-row branch, ignores view.list_item_rects entirely and keeps the pre-M135 hardcoded offset: `let item_idx = y.saturating_sub(3) as usize; app.selected_index = item_idx;` (runner.rs:635-636). That offset only approximates the Milestones/Backlog bordered-table layout. For the Overview/dashboard inbox it is wrong on two counts: (1) the inbox block lives inside the dashboard vertical split (9+5+Min(3) rows), so its first row is far below y=3; (2) each inbox item occupies 3 rows (compute_overview_list_rects emits heights of 1..=3), not 1. So a click in the Overview inbox selects the wrong item or none. For BOARD cards the gap is sharper: compute_board_rects populates view.board_card_rects with per-card rects, but handle_mouse has NO board-card click branch at all — clicking a board card falls into the generic list branch and sets app.selected_index, which is meaningless for the Board lane (board navigation uses board_selected_col/board_selected_card). The pre-computed rects exist but are read only by the AC-01/AC-04 tests, never by the live mouse path. This is exactly the render/hit-test drift L41 describes: the data structure that was supposed to be the single source of truth is computed and then not used for two of the three surfaces. Fix: list-row branch should walk view.list_item_rects and set selected_index to the matched item's position; add a board-card branch that walks view.board_card_rects and sets board_selected_col/board_selected_card. AC-04 ('Clicking on a list row triggers the select action for the item under that row; covers active list, board cards, and any other list-like surface') is not actually met for board cards.
findings.author: external-review (session)
findings.summary: L41 partial: list/board clicks bypass view.list_item_rects/board_card_rects

findings.description: ViewState.overlay_rect is populated by compute_view (view_state.rs:481,549,551) for the help/input/review-menu overlays, but a grep across render.rs and runner.rs shows ZERO reads of overlay_rect in the runtime paths. render() (render.rs:31) still calls render_help_overlay(frame,app,area), render_input_overlay(frame,app,area), render_review_menu_overlay(frame,app,area), and each of those helpers independently re-calls centered_rect(60/50/40, ...) on frame.area() (render.rs:1301,1322,1345) — duplicating the exact math compute_view already performed to produce overlay_rect. So overlay_rect is a dead field whose only consumers are the AC-01/overlay tests. This is (a) the same L41 drift class for overlays (compute_view and the overlay helpers can diverge if one changes the centered_rect percentages and the other does not — there is no test linking them), and (b) dead-code-via-refactor (L13): a field was added to the 'single source of truth' struct but the actual source of truth for overlay geometry remains the scattered centered_rect calls. Fix: either have the overlay helpers read view.overlay_rect (make it the real single source), or drop overlay_rect from ViewState and the tests until M136/M137 wire it. As shipped, the field over-promises: it implies overlays are on the ViewState contract when they are not.
findings.author: external-review (session)
findings.summary: view.overlay_rect is computed by compute_view but never consumed by render() or handle_mouse

findings.description: AC-03 ('clicking a tab ... always selects that tab') and AC-04 ('clicking a list row ... triggers the select action for the item') are verified by tui_view_state.rs::tab_click_hits_rendered_tab, list_row_click_hits_rendered_row, and board_card_click_hits_rendered_card. But these tests NEVER call handle_mouse — the test file itself documents this at line 340-341: 'we exercise the ViewState directly, since handle_mouse is private.' handle_mouse is private (runner.rs:581, no pub), so the tests cannot reach it. They instead assert that view.tab_hit_areas / view.list_item_rects / view.board_card_rects have the right SHAPE (ids, rect heights, ordering) and that the rendered buffer's center cell contains the label. They do NOT assert that dispatching a click at that coordinate actually selects the right item. This is why F-02 went undetected: the board-card test passes because compute_view produces correct board_card_rects, but handle_mouse has no board-card branch and no test can see that. The AC-04 description explicitly says 'Test covers ... board cards, and any other list-like surface' — but board-card selection is untested and, per F-02, unimplemented. This is L15 (tests written against the implementation shape, not the spec's behavioral contract) and L28 (extracted helper tested in isolation, call site still unprotected): the ViewState is the extracted helper; the call site (handle_mouse) is unprotected. Fix: expose a thin test-only dispatch entry point (e.g. pub(crate) handle_mouse_for_test, or make handle_mouse pub(crate)) and add tests that click each rect and assert app.selected_index / board_selected_col+card change to the item under the click. Without that, AC-03/AC-04 are shape-tests masquerading as behavior-tests.
findings.author: external-review (session)
findings.summary: AC-03/AC-04 tests assert ViewState shape, not click dispatch — AC-04 'board cards' false-passes

findings.description: handle_mouse (runner.rs:596-602) constructs the area for compute_view with a hardcoded height:24: `let area = Rect { x:0, y:0, width: term_width, height: 24 };`. The render path (draw_frame, runner.rs:429) correctly uses terminal.size() for BOTH width and height. For the tab-bar hit areas (y=1, single row) this is harmless because tab rects only depend on width. But view.list_item_rects, view.board_card_rects, and view.dashboard_chunks are all height-dependent (compute_overview_list_rects clips items against block_bottom; compute_board_rects sizes card_chunks from inner.height). On a terminal taller or shorter than 24 rows, the ViewState computed on the mouse path describes a DIFFERENT layout than the one the renderer drew. Combined with F-02 (the list branch doesn't use the rects anyway) this is currently latent, but the moment list/board clicks are wired to view.list_item_rects/board_card_rects per F-02's fix, the height:24 placeholder becomes a silent L41 drift source: clicks at the bottom of a 50-row terminal would be tested against a 24-row layout. The comment at runner.rs:594-597 acknowledges 'a placeholder height — only the tab hit areas ... are consulted' but that premise is exactly what F-02 says should change. Fix: thread the real terminal height into handle_mouse (it already receives term_width; add term_height) or, better, have the render pass cache the ViewState and hand it to dispatch so compute_view runs exactly once per frame at the true size (the commit message mentions this was rejected as 'more bookkeeping than it's worth', but that tradeoff was made before the list/board rects were meant to be consumed).
findings.author: external-review (session)
findings.summary: handle_mouse builds the ViewState with a hardcoded height:24, so vertical hit areas are computed against the wrong frame size on non-24-row terminals
